items.title: The actual Gaussian angular component

source.anchor: Section 4.1.1, Eq. (14)–(15) and the following pointwise Gaussian-law sentence
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, CC BY 4.0. ASTIS explanation and formalization; no endorsement implied.

items.statement: In the source construction n is sufficiently large and h=floor((log n)^(1/3)/32). Set K=2^(74(h+1)), P=2^(64(h+1)), S_i=Σ_{j=0}^{h−i}K^j, and a_i,p=1/[p^4 S_i² sqrt((h−i+1)log(2PS_i))]. For 0≤i≤h and even 4≤p≤P, take deterministic unit directions u_i,…,u_h and the ordered tensor ψ_i=u_i⊗u_(i+1)^⊗K⊗⋯⊗u_h^⊗K^(h−i). A standard Gaussian coefficient tensor Ξ_i,p in real Euclidean dimension n^(pS_i) defines F_i,p=√n a_i,p⟨Ξ_i,p,ψ_i^⊗p⟩. At each fixed direction tuple, F_i,p has law N(0,n a_i,p²). The isolated formal identity is valid for every positive n and natural h; joint independence and the degree-summed field are not covered here.
assumptions: n is a positive integer, h a nonnegative integer, 0≤i≤h, and p is even with 4≤p≤P.
The trailing directions u_i,…,u_h are fixed deterministic unit vectors in real Euclidean n-space.
The coefficient block has its unconditioned standard Gaussian probability law; it is not conditioned on admissibility.
The paper fixes sufficiently large n and h=floor((log n)^(1/3)/32). The isolated identity below is proved for every positive n and natural h; this does not extend hard-family admissibility.

formulae.label: Ordered tensor and component
formulae.tex: \psi_i=u_i\otimes u_{i+1}^{\otimes K}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_h^{\otimes K^{h-i}},\qquad F_{i,p}^{\Xi}(u)=\sqrt n\,a_{i,p}\langle\Xi_{i,p},\psi_i(u)^{\otimes p}\rangle.

obligations.label: Realize the ordered tensor polynomial with exact amplitude and coordinate dimension
Derive feature normalization from unit directions
Derive measurability and exact centered Gaussian pushforward law

bindings.boundary: One fixed-direction degree component under its actual standard Gaussian coefficient block. Joint coefficient projection/independence, degree summation, radial fields, adaptive gates, conditional iteration, Lemma 6.2 and all main query lower bounds remain open.

assumption_deltas.source: Sufficiently large n with h=floor((log n)^(1/3)/32) in the hard-family construction
assumption_deltas.reason: This isolated finite Gaussian identity needs neither the large-n threshold nor the prescribed depth. No hard-family admissibility outside the original regime is asserted.

assumption_deltas.source: Even p in {4,6,…,P}, exact K,P,S_i and a_i,p
assumption_deltas.lean: The degree subtype keeps parity and both endpoints; the literal body keeps every constant
assumption_deltas.reason: No amplitude bound, approximated constant, or off-domain division fallback replaces the source formula.

assumption_deltas.source: Ordered real tensor space of dimension n^(pS_i)
assumption_deltas.lean: EuclideanSpace ℝ ((Fin p × Σ j, Fin(K^j)) → Fin n)
assumption_deltas.reason: Slots enumerate all repeated factors and coordinates choose one entry per factor. The focused universal cardinality test establishes the exact dimension; no symmetric-tensor normalization is used.

assumption_deltas.source: Angular function on a product of unit spheres
assumption_deltas.lean: Same polynomial extends to arbitrary direction vectors
assumption_deltas.reason: The extension is explicit and uses the identical formula without a fallback. The adjacent probability-law theorem is restricted to the original sphere domain.
